description:
The village of Mcely appears in a parchment of 1252. In 1698 Count Octavian Ladislav of Waldstein built a Baroque hunting château here. Baron Jan Filip Wessenberg-Ampringen bought it in 1808, and in 1841 the dilapidated Baroque building was rebuilt as a new residence in an austere classical style.

In 1869 Count Filip Boos-Waldeck sold the estate to Prince Hugo Maxmilian of the Thurn-Taxis family, which had its principal seat in nearby Loučeň; the prince and his descendants owned Mcely until 1948. In 1903 the west wing was demolished because of its poor foundations, and a costly renovation followed when Prince Erich Thurn-Taxis married Countess Gabriela Kinsky.

After 1948 the château was used by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the Ministry of the Interior and was left in a dilapidated state. A demanding renovation began on 15 June 2004, led by Inéz and James Cusumano; the château opened to its first guests in 2006, and the Mcely Bouquet spa followed in 2010. Today it is a five-star hotel with an English park, a restaurant and a spa.

faqs.question: Who owned Mcely Château?
faqs.answer: Count Octavian Ladislav of Waldstein built it in 1698, and from 1869 to 1948 it belonged to the Thurn-Taxis family, whose principal seat was nearby Loučeň.

faqs.question: When did Mcely Château open as a hotel?
faqs.answer: The château was renovated from 2004 and opened to its first guests in 2006; a spa followed in 2010.

hotel.room_location_note: Rooms are at Chateau Mcely, Mcely 61; the estate also has other accommodation, so ask the hotel which building your room is in
hotel.how_to_stay:
**Getting there:** At Mcely 61, in the village of Mcely in Central Bohemia, about 5 km from the Thurn-Taxis seat at Loučeň; Booking lists free on-site parking with valet service and electric charging.

**Rooms & rates:** From approx. €184/night for a Superior Double Room with air conditioning, a private bathroom, a minibar and free Wi-Fi, with breakfast, one hour of spa time a day, valet parking and high-speed internet included on the non-refundable rate seen; a free-cancellation rate was around €230 and a Luxury Suite around €400. Booking shows a small tax charge (about €1) separately.

**On-site:** A spa, a restaurant, an English park and free parking.

**Good to know:** Rates were seen for one February 2027 stay, a low-season date, so check your own dates on Booking. The estate also has other accommodation besides the château, so ask the hotel which building your room is in.

**Combine with:** [Loučeň Château](/castles/czech-republic/loucen-castle), the Thurn-Taxis family seat a few kilometres away.
